title: 2997. Minimum Number of Operations to Make Array XOR Equal to K

examples.explanation: We can do the following operations: - Choose element 2 which is 3 == (011)2, we flip the first bit and we obtain (010)2 == 2. nums becomes [2,1,2,4]. - Choose element 0 which is 2 == (010)2, we flip the third bit and we obtain (110)2 = 6. nums becomes [6,1,2,4]. The XOR of elements of the final array is (6 XOR 1 XOR 2 XOR 4) == 1 == k. It can be shown that we cannot make the XOR equal to k in less than 2 operations.
The XOR of elements of the array is (2 XOR 0 XOR 2 XOR 0) == 0 == k. So no operation is needed.
